chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The limit of the one who despairs from menstruation is fifty years.
ai.seo_question: What is the age limit for menopause in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes fifty years as the definitive age limit (ya's) for menopause, a ruling primarily attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) that serves as a standard in Shia jurisprudence for determining when menstrual impurity (hayd) ceases permanently. While some jurists allow for earlier cessation if confirmed by observation, this fixed age provides a clear legal boundary for marital status and ritual purity obligations. The narration highlights the practical application of prophetic tradition in codifying biological transitions within Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A limit of the one who despairs from the menstruation (Haydh) is fifty years (of age)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Menopause happens at the age of fifty years.”’
